correctness.rationale: For prime p≥5, a sum of pth roots with total p terms is zero iff each residue occurs once, via irreducibility of Φ_p. At translation a≠0, recentering x by a/2 converts the quartic difference plus bx to 4a y³+(a³+b)y+constant. The collision conic x²+xy+y²=-c has p−χ(-3) solutions and at most two diagonal, so y³+cy permutes only for c=0 and p≡2 mod3. This gives the full two-branch zero set and Weyl rank. For fourth moment, Fourier autocorrelation of the cubic phase difference has quadratic difference with coefficient 12ah≠0, whose Gauss sum squared modulus is p, yielding sum|A|^4=3−3/p+1/p². Parseval and Cauchy imply constant-modulus bound 2−1/p, achieved by cubic chirp; quartic excess (1−1/p)². Independent exact cyclotomic histograms across six primes and complex fourth-moment evaluations agree, but analytic Gauss/conic arguments cover all primes.
